newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Chrysler's Lutz says electric cars 10-15 years off.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler's Lutz says electric cars 10-15 years off.

text.p: Chrysler Corp vice chairman Robert Lutz, complaining about the media building up hopes for electric cars, said on Monday he believed the required battery technology was still 10 to 15 years away.

Lutz, a long-time Detroit car industry executive, also said countries must re-examine the benefits of electric vehicles as a way to reduce pollution, saying an electric vehicle could often be more damaging to the environment.
"We are all for it but the battery technology is 10 to 15 years away," Lutz told a luncheon at the American International Club in Geneva, a day before the start of the Geneva car show.

But he added, "It is my real belief that if we had not discovered the internal combustion engine, and we were all driving around in electric cars, we would now be hailing the gasoline engine as a breakthrough that is going to help us solve a lot of our environmental items."

Lutz said said an electric car that derived its power from coal-powered electric plants had more environmental impact than a gasoline-powered car due to the use of coal, the loss of power over transmission lines and lead in batteries.
"Unless it is a country that produces all its electricity by hydro-electric means, the electric car hurts more than it helps," Lutz said.
Chrylser has signed on to a consortium with other major U.S. carmakers and battery manufacturers to produce suitable batteries for electric vehicles -- a breakthrough that has so far been lacking.

He specifically criticised the U.S. media for building up hopes about breakthroughs in technology that would allow efficient use of battery-powered cars, which have so far been limited by battery weight and capacity.
Lutz said the current range of batteries under development were cost-prohibitive and unsuitable for production.
